function.name: execute
function.description: Run any shell command in a working directory (defaults to the project root) and see stdout, stderr, and exit code. Large output may be truncated to a head+tail preview with metadata. Don't background with &; use task_create.

description.description: What this command does, in a few words (what, not why). Shown to the user as the step's title, so include it on every call.

cwd.description: Optional working directory to run in (defaults to the project root). Relative paths are resolved against the project root.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file from disk. Large files may be truncated to a head+tail preview with metadata. Optionally pass start_line and end_line (1-based, inclusive) to read only a specific line range. An image file (png, jpeg, gif, webp) comes back as the picture itself: read it to see it.

start_line.description: Optional start line (1-based, inclusive). Without end_line, reads to the end of the file.

end_line.description: Optional end line (1-based, inclusive). Without start_line, reads from line 1.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file (parent directories are created automatically)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit an existing file. Mode 1 (default): replace an exact old_text block with new_text, where old_text must appear exactly once. Mode 2 (range): when start_line and end_line are provided, replace that whole line range with new_text.

old_text.description: Exact text to replace (required in exact-match mode)

start_line.description: Optional start line (1-based, inclusive) for range mode. Must be provided with end_line.

end_line.description: Optional end line (1-based, inclusive) for range mode. Must be provided with start_line.

function.name: memory_read
function.description: Read a memory entry from scoped memories. Scope is optional: if omitted, read falls back from project to system. Leave name blank to read indexes.

name.description: Memory entry name without .md extension; leave blank for indexes

function.name: memory_write
function.description: Write or update a memory entry in scoped memories. Scope is required: project or system. Use the `name` parameter for the entry name (use `name`, NOT `path` — the file tools use `path`); each scope's index.md is auto-maintained (one managed line per entry); use name "index" to write the index file verbatim. For a small change to an existing memory (a step, a line), `edit` its file (<scope dir>/<name>.md) instead of rewriting it all; its index line is refreshed either way. If the user asks to save guidance for the current model only, pass current_model_only: true to save a model-specific overlay.

scope.description: Scope to write into: project or system

description.description: Optional short description appended to the managed index line

current_model_only.description: Set true to save this entry as a model-specific overlay for the current model only (<name>.<model>.md); it is auto-appended when the entry is read under that model and never listed in the index.

function.name: task_create
function.description: Start a background task for a long-running shell command. Servers and anything meant to keep running belong here, not in execute with &. Returns task id and output path for later inspection.

command.description: Shell command to run in the background

cwd.description: Optional working directory (defaults to project root)

env.description: Optional JSON object of environment overrides; use this for PATH or tool-specific variables

function.name: task_get
function.description: Get full metadata for a task by id. Use read on output_path to inspect command output.

function.name: task_list
function.description: List all background tasks in the current workspace with current status.

function.name: task_stop
function.description: Stop a running background task by id.

function.name: task_wait
function.description: Wait for a background task to finish. Polls every 0.5s until completion, a log pattern matches, or timeout. Timed-out waits include a bounded output tail.

tail_lines.description: Log lines to return when timing out or matching a pattern (default: 10, max: 100)

done_pattern.description: Optional regular expression that returns early when it matches the recent log output

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch the content of a URL (HTML or text) and return cleaned text. Handles HTML by stripping scripts/styles and extracting visible text. Returns error messages for invalid URLs or HTTP errors.

function.name: register_reminder
function.description: Register a periodic reminder. The harness injects a [SYSTEM:] message into your next idle turn when the reminder is due.

description.description: What should happen when this reminder fires

interval_minutes.description: How often to remind (1-1440 minutes, i.e. up to 1 day)

function.name: cancel_reminder
function.description: Cancel a previously registered reminder so it stops firing.

function.name: list_reminders
function.description: List all active registered reminders.

function.name: list_sessions
function.description: List the other chi sessions of this project (newest first, up to 20): id, whether a worker runs it, its folder and last prompt; other projects: cwd "/". Use it to find the session send_note should go to.

cwd.description: Only sessions in this folder or below it, in any project (optional)

function.name: send_note
function.description: Send a context note to another chi session: background information it sees on its next turn, attributed to this session. It does not start a turn there or ask it to do anything.

session.description: The target session's id or a unique prefix of it (from list_sessions)

text.description: The note: what the other session should know (up to 16 KiB)

function.name: delegate
function.description: Hand a task to a child chi session that runs in parallel in this folder and returns only its final reply (its trace stays out of this context). The child is a normal session: it shows in the lists as a child of this one and the user can attach to it. With session, send a follow-up to one of this session's children instead. A tool call the child needs approved goes to your user as one of your own approvals; you only see how it was answered, as a line in the result. Children keep running if this turn is canceled. With wait false, chi brings each child's reply to you by itself when the child ends its turn (a delegate report, also when you are idle): don't poll it with delegate_result. To retry or redirect a child, use delegate with its session (task_* tools are for background commands, not sessions). A child stays until stopped: once its work is done, stop it with execute `chi sessions stop ID` (a follow-up with session wakes it again).

task.description: The task, as the child's first message: self-contained, with what to report back

model.description: The child's model (a name or alias; default: this session's)

session.description: A child's id or prefix: send the task there as a follow-up instead of starting a new child

wait.description: Wait for the reply (default true); false returns at once so several children can run side by side

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait (default: 600; 0 checks once without waiting); a timed-out child keeps running

function.name: delegate_result
function.description: Wait for a delegated child session's next reply: the child named, or this session's newest running child (name the child when a delegate report is about it). A delegate report already carries the reply: don't call this for it. Returns early if the child waits for a question the user must answer. A tool call the child needs approved goes to your user while this waits; the result says how it was answered.

session.description: The child's id or prefix (default: the newest running child)

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait (default: 600; 0 checks once without waiting)

function.name: ask_user_question
function.description: Ask the user a structured qualification question. Supports single/multi selection plus optional freeform/Other input. Prefer this over plain numbered lists when you need a clear choice. The harness renders it natively and returns {selected, freeform}.

question.description: The question to ask the user

multi_select.description: Allow selecting multiple options (comma-separated in TUI). Default false.

allow_freeform.description: Allow freeform/Other text alongside selection. Default false.
